status_detail: County EDC site reviewed; broad web/news search found only social-media discussion and moratorium chatter, with no confirmed project record, developer, site application, tax abatement, or county planning item located.
notes: Crawford County Economic Development markets industrial land near I-64 but does not identify a data center project. Unverified Facebook/YouTube references were not treated as project evidence.

status_detail: Outrigger Industrial presented preliminary plans for a 120-acre data center at the southeast corner of I-69 and US 50 in March 2026; Washington City Council voted unanimously on May 11, 2026 to stop dealings with Outrigger and explore a moratorium after unanswered utility/use questions.
notes: Capacity cited as upper end of reported 250-500 MW estimate from Indiana Public Media; WAMW also reported 100 MW to 1 GW range. Buildings were estimated at $100M-$250M plus $500M-$1B equipment, with 100-150 employees.

status_detail: County adopted/reviewed a temporary data center moratorium, but official minutes and local coverage indicate no formal data center proposal had been brought forward at the time of review.
notes: Official DeKalb materials discuss data center ordinance/moratorium work; a meeting record notes officials answered that they had not had discussions for a data center to come to DeKalb County.

status_detail: Dearborn County imposed a moratorium on rezoning applications for commercial solar, BESS, and data centers and is collecting ordinance comments, but no specific data center project application was located.
notes: News and county pages frame the data-center action as regulatory preparation; known development pressure in the county appears centered on solar rather than a named data center project.

status_detail: Greensburg City Council approved a 550-acre Economic Revitalization Area and a 10-year, 60% real property tax abatement for Jumping Bison LLC in December 2024; city later described the project as a two-phase, American-owned data center at $400M per phase.
notes: Official city State of the City confirms the data-center deal and two $400M phases. Capacity is from Cleanview/tracker; other public reporting emphasizes 550 acres and $800M rather than MW.

aliases: Muncie Industria Centre data center qualified site
status_detail: Indiana Michigan Power announced in 2013 that a Muncie Industria Centre site received a third-party Data Center Qualified designation and was being marketed for mission-critical/data center use; no specific tenant/developer project was found in 2026 searches.
notes: Included under wide-net criteria as a certified/marketed data-center-ready site, not a confirmed build. I&M described a test-model mission-critical facility with 100,000 square feet of raised floor; local 2026 coverage says county officials are courting interested companies.

status_detail: County/city searches found discussion of how Huntingburg and Dubois County should regulate data centers, but no named commercial data center project, site application, developer, permit, or tax abatement.
notes: Huntingburg officials distinguished existing internal bank/manufacturer data rooms from large-scale commercial facilities; no hyperscale/colocation project was identified.

developer: Jones Petrie Rafinski / Wilhelm and Kauffman trusts
status_detail: Elkhart County Advisory Plan Commission recommended denial of DPUD-0340-2026 on July 9, 2026; the petitioner then requested withdrawal on August 3 and Bristol Town Council packet/resolution acknowledged withdrawal of the rezoning application on August 6, 2026.
notes: Planning materials say a data center could still be built on approximately 400 acres already zoned M-1, but the broader A-1/M-1 to DPUD M-1 rezoning for Bristol Innovation Park was recommended for denial and withdrawn.

status_detail: IURC testimony and tracker/news sources identify Takanock as developing a data center project in Elkhart County/Goshen; later public summaries indicate the project is stalled or abandoned due to NIPSCO/GenCo power-service disputes, but no final county denial was found.
notes: Capacity uses upper-end public tracker figure; Baxtel describes 250 MW to 1,500 MW. ProjectBeckham.com is an independent information site, not official, so IURC filings are the stronger primary evidence that Takanock was developing an Elkhart County data center.

status_detail: County records show commissioners discussed/supporting data center openness and later data center moratorium hearings, but no specific Fayette County Indiana project, developer, site application, permit, or abatement was verified.
notes: A 37-acre/300,000-sf social/news search hit referred to Fayetteville, Georgia rather than Fayette County, Indiana, so it was excluded.

status_detail: Regional reporting says Floyd County is updating zoning language for possible data centers and New Albany enacted/advanced a temporary ban, but no confirmed Floyd County data center project was found.
notes: LPM identified confirmed nearby projects in Clark County/Jeffersonville and Charlestown, not Floyd County; Floyd County and New Albany discussion appears preventative/regulatory.
